claims.why_not_priced: The mispricing is in the size, not just the sign. A 3.5% implied move against a 7.1% eight-quarter realised median means the option market is charging half of what this name actually does on prints, and it is doing so into the single most consequential disclosure of the year - the quarter in which a multi-billion-renminbi penalty lands and management has to say what a monopoly determination does to take rates. Nothing in this 38-item capture engages with that: there is no sell-side note, no consensus revenue figure and no company document, and the only substantive commentary is a valuation case (6.9x TTM earnings, $17 a share of cash, book value $36 against a $43.84 price) that treats the penalty as a one-off. Call volume leading puts 8:3 says the positioning is on the recovery side. I sign it negative but small because the price has already absorbed a 44.48% drawdown to within 22% of book, which is a real floor, and because international bookings growing 65-90% is a genuine offset.
